sn4.13:2.1: Māra thinks that “drunk on poetry” (_kāveyyamatta_, see [sn8.12:2.1]()) means literally drunk. In Rig Veda 10.131.4, Indra, drunk on an excess of _soma_, needs the illicit beer of Namuci (= Māra) to revive him. Perhaps we see in this phrase an echo of the Vedic tradition of taking intoxicants so that the god speaks through you in inspired verse.
sn4.13:2.2: sampacura and pacura in relation to attha occur at AN 7.64, AN 4.53, AN 4.55, AN 5.148. The sense is clarified at AN 5.148 where it is the result of generosity, i.e. if you give, then later on you will not go without. This sense makes sense in all contexts, so should be translated accordingly.
